_note: Runnable command blocks per session id, merged into curriculum/*.md by scripts/build_curriculum.py. Every block is real: it executes against open-weight models (via Ollama/LiteLLM) or open-source CNCF tooling. Nothing here is pseudo-code.

_conventions.model_endpoint: All model calls go through an OpenAI-compatible base URL so no lab hard-codes a provider. Default is local Ollama at http://localhost:11434/v1 (see MODELS.md).

M0.1.goal: Show that autonomy lives in the action plane, not the model.
run: ollama pull llama3.3 && ollama pull nomic-embed-text
# same prompt, three configurations: bare model / read-only tools / write tools
M0.1.expect: Identical model output; only configuration 3 changes state on disk. Prints a PASS/FAIL table.

M0.2.goal: Build the minimum loop and prove the verifier is the security control.
run: python3 loop.py --task fix-tests --verifier pytest      # honest oracle
python3 loop.py --task fix-tests --verifier none        # no stop signal
M0.2.expect: pytest verifier converges or stops; llm-judge declares success on broken code; none diverges until the budget kills it.

M0.3.goal: Walk one workflow up the autonomy ladder with named promotion evidence.
M0.3.expect: L2.5 refuses to run until the promotion evidence file exists — autonomy as an earned event.

M0.4.goal: Reproduce direct and indirect injection, then measure a real defense.
run: cd labs/m0-injection && python3 poison.py --target rag   # plant in a retrieved doc
python3 poison.py --target rag --defense tagging   # re-run with untrusted-content tagging
M0.4.expect: Attack success rate drops measurably with tagging; the number, not the vibe, is the deliverable.

M0.5.goal: Locate yourself on the ownership map.
run: $EDITOR my-org-ownership.csv   # fill Owns / Builds / Uses for your function
M0.5.expect: Every topic cluster has exactly one owner. Any row with zero or two owners is your first finding.

A1.2.goal: Stand up the whole reference control plane locally.
run: kubectl apply -k opa/       # policy decision point
A1.2.expect: verify.sh fails loudly if any layer is advisory rather than enforcing.

A1.3.goal: Make the over-privileged grant structurally unrepresentable.
run: python3 prove_unrepresentable.py   # attempts to write the bad grant
A1.3.expect: The bad grant is rejected by the schema, not by a policy check that could be skipped.

A2.2.goal: Issue a workload identity with zero static secrets.
run: kubectl exec -n spire spire-server-0 -- /opt/spire/bin/spire-server entry create \
./show-svid.sh   # fetch and decode the SVID from inside the workload
A2.2.expect: A short-lived SVID appears with no secret ever written to disk; re-attests automatically after rotation.

A2.5.goal: A three-hop delegation chain that survives audit.
run: python3 decode_chain.py token.jwt  # prints the nested act claim chain
A2.5.expect: Each hop shows a nested `act` claim and a strictly smaller scope. Attenuation is visible in the token, not asserted in a doc.

A2.8.goal: Cut standing access to zero so an injection has nothing to spend.
run: ./jit.sh --status    # authority exists only inside the window
A2.8.expect: Authority is absent before and after the window; the agent literally cannot spend what it does not hold.

A3.1.goal: Measure escape surface across three sandbox tiers.
A3.1.expect: A table of syscall surface and reachable host resources per tier — a number you can put in a design review.

A3.2.goal: Prove an agent with no egress control has no other meaningful control.
A3.2.expect: Identical agent, identical payload; the only variable is egress policy.

A3.6.goal: Build the five containment levers before you need them.
A3.6.expect: Each lever fires under load and is timed. A lever that only works when idle is not a lever.

B1.1.goal: Cut the false-positive rate with reachability reasoning, and measure it.
B1.1.expect: Prints precision before/after triage. The FP rate — not the detection rate — is the number that moved.

B1.3.goal: Never raise a PR for a patch you did not build and test.
run: # generates -> compiles -> runs tests -> only then writes patch.diff
B1.3.expect: Patches failing the local build are discarded before a human ever sees them; acceptance rate is printed.

B1.5.goal: Watch your own review harness obey an injected instruction, then close it.
run: git apply injected-pr.diff       # a PR containing an instruction to the reviewer
B1.5.expect: The unprotected run emits the attacker's verdict; the tagged run does not.

B2.1.goal: One scaffold, swappable model, unchanged loop.
B2.1.expect: Identical loop code, three backbones, comparable traces — the prerequisite for C2.6 multi-backbone benchmarking.

B2.2.goal: Show a same-family judge grading its own homework.
run: # then compare with a judge drawn from the same family as the generator
B2.2.expect: The oracle and the same-family judge disagree in a specific, reproducible direction.

B2.4.goal: Bound a divergent loop four different ways.
B2.4.expect: Four different stop reasons, all recorded in the trace. 'It finished' is never one of them.

B2.10.goal: The full eval harness: ground truth, blind protocol, execution-verified scoring, model comparison.
run: scripts/vulnbench.sh build      # 552-row ground truth: SecLLMHolmes + TerraGoat/Checkov
scripts/vulnbench.sh verify     # regression fingerprint, expect Expert Accuracy 0.9479
scripts/vulnbench.sh compare    # blind model comparison across backbones
scripts/vulnbench.sh cybergym-preflight   # can this host run execution benchmarks?
B2.10.expect: Real numbers with committed evidence: per-model precision/recall/F1/Expert Accuracy, plus the failing-question list. This lab is fully built and tested — see its README for the recorded results.

C1.1.goal: Drive a planner/executor pair against a local target you own.
run: docker compose up -d dvwa juice-shop     # local targets only
C1.1.expect: Attack chains, not payload suggestions. scope.yaml is enforced by the harness — out-of-scope hosts are refused.

C1.3.goal: Run a real injection campaign and get a success rate.
C1.3.expect: A measured attack-success-rate per probe family, per model — comparable across Llama / GLM / Kimi.

C1.6.goal: Game the eval deliberately, then close the hole you used.
run: scripts/vulnbench.sh compare   # see the inflated number
C1.6.expect: You reproduce an inflated score, then patch the harness so the same trick fails.

C2.2.goal: Chart jailbreak taxonomy differences across three open-weight families.
run: for M in llama3.3 glm-4.6 kimi-k2; do garak --model_type openai.OpenAICompatible --model_name $M --probes dan,encoding,malwaregen --report_prefix $M; done
C2.2.expect: Per-family refusal and elicitation profiles. Model effects separated from harness effects.

C2.6.goal: Separate model effects from harness effects.
run: for M in llama3.3 glm-4.6 kimi-k2; do MODEL=$M scripts/vulnbench.sh compare; done
C2.6.expect: Same harness, three backbones — the delta is the model. This is exactly how the committed comparison table was produced.

D1.1.goal: Supervise a triage loop by exception rather than by re-reading.
D1.1.expect: The loop clears the known-benign and escalates the rest with its reasoning attached.

D1.4.goal: Five detections whose subject is a non-human principal.
run: ./install-sigma.sh   # scope drift, tool-sequence anomaly, off-hours autonomy, retrieval anomaly, NHI-at-human-time
D1.4.expect: All five fire on synthetic-but-real agent telemetry from the A3/B2 labs.

D1.6.goal: Tell an agent apart from the human whose credential it inherited.
D1.6.expect: A working classifier — your earliest Shadow Autonomy signal.

D2.2.goal: Attribute an incident to an agent, an authority and a delegation chain.
D2.2.expect: Names the agent, the delegated authority, the hop where scope widened, and the prompt that started it.

D2.4.goal: Exercise the containment ladder in order, against a live misbehaving agent.
D2.4.expect: Each lever is timed; revocation hits one agent without collateral (the A2.4 deliverable, proven here).

D2.5.goal: Replay an agent run to a regulator-grade standard.
D2.5.expect: The run reproduces, or the tool tells you exactly which field was never logged to make replay possible.

E1.2.goal: Discover agents you did not know you had.
E1.2.expect: A register built from telemetry rather than from a survey nobody answered.

E1.5.goal: Turn an eval report into audit evidence — and find how it could mislead you.
run: python3 ../e1-grc/challenge.py --pack evidence/AI-EVAL-01.json   # the three ways this misleads
E1.5.expect: An OSCAL-shaped evidence pack, plus a written challenge: best-of-k reporting, conformance-as-accuracy, and judge dependence.

E1.7.goal: Automate the evidence package, not the judgment.
E1.7.expect: Control drift surfaces as a diff; a human still decides what it means.

E1.8.goal: Run a real AIBOM against a model artefact.
run: cosign verify-blob --bundle model.sig model.gguf   # provenance where signed
E1.8.expect: An artefact inventory with provenance status per component — and an honest 'unsigned' where that is the truth.

E2.5.goal: Redact inside the trust boundary before anything crosses out.
E2.5.expect: PII is removed before egress; the redaction decision is logged as evidence for E2.7.

E2.8.goal: Build the audit trail out of the delegation chain itself.
E2.8.expect: Which agent, under whose authority, in what scope, verified by which control, reviewable by whom — all from the `act` chain.

E3.5.goal: Instrument the six board-level metrics from your own lab stack.
E3.5.expect: Inventory coverage, attested-identity share, standing-access reduction, MTT-revoke, blast-radius distribution, eval-gate pass rate.
